evidence: src/pool.ts:1129, new in this round (25dcb79): `runGit(contextDir, ["worktree", "list", "--porcelain", "-z"])`, read only inside `if (listed.status === 0)` (src/pool.ts:1130). On any nonzero exit the loop is skipped and branchCheckedOutAt stays undefined. That value is the ONLY guard against deleting a branch another worktree has checked out: stage 3 deletes with update-ref, which does not check worktrees (src/pool.ts:1203-1215).

`git worktree list` has no -z before git 2.36. Measured with git 2.34.1, the packaged git of Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (git_2.34.1-1ubuntu1.17_amd64.deb from archive.ubuntu.com, extracted into scratch and run through a wrapper, never installed): `git worktree list --porcelain -z` prints `error: unknown switch `z'` and exits 129; without -z it exits 0. The kernel declares no git floor: doctor's git check passes on presence alone (src/commands/doctor.ts:216-222).

The shipped test test/pool.test.ts:684 (`pool destroy refuses with one reason line when the task branch cannot be deleted`, the CR-201 refusal), run in a scratch clone at ea3edb3, node v26.6.0: git 2.43.0 pass (tests 1, pass 1); git 2.34.1 first on PATH FAIL (tests 1, pass 0, fail 1); git 2.34.1 with ONLY the listing reverted to the pre-round form (no -z, newline split) pass. The only variable between the last two runs is this round's change.

Effect, a probe test added only in that scratch clone (a foreign worktree at `<own>-foreign` holding task/t-pf, then `tiphys pool destroy --task t-pf`): git 2.43.0, destroy exit 1 with `cannot delete branch task/t-pf: it is checked out at .../worktrees/t-pf-foreign; remove that worktree first`; git 2.34.1, destroy exit 0, `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/task/t-pf` exit 1 (branch deleted) and `rev-parse --verify HEAD` in the foreign worktree exit 128 (left on a dangling HEAD); git 2.34.1 with the pre-round listing, refused, exit 1, branch kept.

Why no gate or test in CI sees it: CI runners carry a git newer than 2.36, and the round's own named test (test/pool.test.ts:431) fails on git 2.34.1 at its capture replay (`git worktree list --porcelain -z: error: unknown switch 'z'`, actual 129, expected 0) before it reaches destroy. The round's other five named tests pass on git 2.34.1 (tests 6, pass 5, fail 1, the one being test/pool.test.ts:431): `diff -z`, `diff --cached -z` and `ls-tree -z` are old flags.

Mechanism: a flag added to a git call whose failure is silently tolerated, without asking whether every git the kernel runs under accepts it. The `if (listed.status === 0)` arm predates the round (it is at b63cb44); the round made it reachable on a stock LTS git. The round's D2 derivation asked whether each listing needs -z and did not ask whether -z exists for that subcommand; `src/pool.ts:1129` is the only site among the seven where the answer is no.
findings.concrete-fix: Make a failed worktree listing refuse the destroy: record it as indeterminate (as branchTip already is) and refuse in evaluateDestroy when the branch is present and the listing could not be read. Then keep the newline fix without depending on git 2.36: either declare git >= 2.36 as a floor that doctor FAILs below, or fall back to the newline listing when git refuses -z and refuse when a listed path cannot be trusted. Add a named test in which the listing fails (a PATH git wrapper replaying git 2.34.1's real refusal of -z, recorded as a capture) asserting that destroy refuses and the branch survives; witness it red against the current `if (listed.status === 0)` arm.
findings.analysis: Introduced by this fix round (25dcb79). Graded by the rubric: a guard on a destructive operation passes while its subject is broken. The path is a stock Ubuntu 22.04 LTS git (2.34.1) plus a task branch checked out in another worktree, which is exactly the situation the guard exists for. The second condition narrows the path, so medium, not high. The consequence is a ref deletion that strands another worktree on a dangling HEAD; its recoverability was not measured.
